original.title: Near-top fresh labels admit only disjoint adjacent swaps
original.statement: The row-h column order on [max(h+1,T(h−1)+1),r−2] is increasing up to disjoint adjacent-value swaps.
assumptions: Record-tight E=F=0 branch and the explicit near-top fresh-label interval.

exactAuditedStatement: In a record-tight E=F=0 birth h with r=sigma_h and m=T(h-1), the row-h subsequence of labels F=[max(h+1, m+1), r-2], ordered by physical source column, is the increasing list up to disjoint adjacent-value swaps.
hypotheses: Record H(h)=0 and gap/tight context; F may be empty or singleton.
Claim concerns only F, allowing historical/outside-F labels to interleave. The main terminal-capacity argument uses h>=3; h=1,2 are checked separately below.
proofDependencyMap: Shared canonical foundation: exact positive-MEX/COPY recurrence and P01-P12, independently reconstructed in ../CANONICAL-FOUNDATIONS.md with exact declaration mapping and game interpretation. DEPENDENCIES.json records the additional service lemmas. Final kernel receipts bind the source versions.
ROW-SHARP, tight survivor roster, terminal capacity proved above; full source-time proof support independently read.
independentDerivationAndChecks: E0 implies every future d(j)>d(h): ROW-SHARP gives d(j)>=2j+1-A(j)>=d(h)+(j-h) using A one-Lipschitz. Record and r blocker give T(h)<=r-1. If h blocker, ROW-SHARP at h-1 gives d(h-1)>=r, impossible; thus h diagonal and d(h-1)=r-1, E(h-1)=0.

If y=v(h)<r, the r-y higher awards require r-y distinct earlier y sources by terminal capacity. Earlier diagonals lie<=r-1 and are distinct, allowing only r-1-y. Contradiction; v(h)=r. Since no old host dies at h, continuing hosts V=U minus{h-1} have full rosters[h, r-2] before and[h+1, r-1] after.

For y in F, every earlier row before h-1 has maximum<=m<y, so the only old journal containing y at h is its unique row h-1 service host k_y. It is not a seed: earlier diagonals<=m, birth diagonals r-1, r+1 are outside F, and future diagonals>r+1. All F labels are therefore blockers.

If a higher current award z precedes current y, MEX forces y into that host journal, so that host is k_y. Thus y has at most one larger F predecessor. One host cannot skip two F labels since its only new pre-row h award was one value, so each z has at most one smaller F successor.

Inversion graph of the F permutation has degree<=1 at both endpoints. An inversion between values with an intermediate value b would force a second inversion at one endpoint: b lies before the lower endpoint or after the higher endpoint. Therefore every inversion is between numerically adjacent F values and such pairs are disjoint. Empty/singleton intervals satisfy the statement vacuously. No hostwise+1 conclusion follows.

Small indices do not b or row the q>=3 terminal-capacity lemma. Column 0 is immortal by the exact rail. The literal first rows give h=1, r=2, d(1)=3 and an empty F interval, so the conclusion is vacuous. For h=2, E=F=0 would force r=3 from d(2)=4 and A(2)=1, contradicting the q=3 penultimate no-death theorem. Thus no omitted small tight case remains.
